Tolson had pulled a muscle, Norman Caves had contracted tonsilitis, Andorka was sitting very important exams and Mal Ash threatened to retire; I was unable to change his mind.
An excellent start to the season was made by Norman Caves in the triple jump with 45'4", only 13" less than his highly ranked best of last year.

McCorquindale were competing elsewhere, and with Stan Vickers Eric Hall, Norman Caves, Mal Ash and Andorka also unavailable our team could not be said to be truly representative of the name of Belgrave.

Norman Caves made the total four for Belgrave by yet again winning the triple jump with 43'6". In the Middlesex Championships at Enfield Dave Ansell was once more amongst the leading long jumpers and finished second with 21'5¼".

Norman Caves was in excellent form winning the high-jump with 584" and the hop-step & jump with 44'10". The ever present Jim McGrath was second to Norman in the high-jump, and also the shot, and it was most pleaseing to see Andorka competing once more after examinations, to win the shot with a putt of 43'1½".
In the "Charlie Cook Cup", Norman Caves was successful with a Triple Jump of 44'11½". Second was Charlie Jones (43'0½") whilst a newcomer of very great promise in A.Underwood jumped 42 ft.

Norman Caves's early effort of 46'5" in the Triple Jump gave promise of great things but he suffered injury and it was not until late in the season that he came back with performances nearing his best.

Our only winner in the trophy events was Norman Caves, who took the HSJ with a distance of 45'-0". But there was a definite all-round improvement on last year's effort, for every one of our team was placed in the first six in his event; we thus gained 21 points against last year's total of nine.

This year's effort read, 100 yds---10.2, 220yds---22.2, 440yds---49.4---great running, from a fine athlete. Norman Caves, HSJ title holder, did not compete this year as he wishes to exercise a Surrey residential qualification in 1961.

After a winning leap of 19'6½" in the long jump Norman Caves also came near to a double, clearing 5'5" for second place in the high jump. Details of the Youth's match can be found with the rest of their news on Page 9.

His victory in the long jump was no surprise, for with the absence of his "twin", Dave Ansell, Jim's only serious rival was Norman Caves; although young Derek Wade gave them both a scare by recording six valid jumps between 18'3½" and 18'10".

In a Bedfordshire v Hertfordshire match on May 21st Peter Eldridge won the 220 and 440 with 22.8 and 48.9, Norman Caves won the long jump and HSJ with 20"8' and 46'4', whilst Alan Spicer's 16.2 placed him 2nd in the 120yds hurdles-----A BELGRAVE field day!
